name: 宮島咖喱麵麭研究所 宮島本店 (Miyajima Curry Pan Kenkyujo Miyajima Honten)

claims.text: All products are wheat-flour curry breads fried in a shared kitchen, so there is no gluten-free safe option.
Signature items contain oysters (shellfish) and other varieties contain wagyu beef; breads are not plant-based.
The grilled oysters are finished with soy-butter, miso-butter and lemon-soy-butter sauces, which use standard wheat-based Japanese soy sauce and miso.
Anago-meshi and the rice sets are seasoned with Japanese soy-sauce-based tare, which standardly contains wheat; no wheat-free seasoning is mentioned.
Menu is centered on conger eel and oysters with fish-based seasonings; no vegan or vegetarian items are listed.
Anago rice and oyster bowls are seasoned with sweet soy-based tare/soy sauce, which in standard Japanese cooking is wheat-based.

name: もみじ饅頭 木村屋 (Momiji Manju Kimuraya)

claims.text: All momiji manju are baked from a shared wheat-flour batter on the same griddle, so the entire product line contains gluten with no gluten-free preparation.
The batter is egg- and flour-based and fillings include dairy cream cheese, custard, and chocolate; bean-paste versions share the same egg-flour shell, so there is no vegan-safe item.

name: 紅葉堂 弐番屋 (Momijido Nibanya)

claims.text: The shop deep-fries wheat-batter momiji manju; there is no gluten-free menu and no published statement about a dedicated fryer, so cross-contamination should be assumed.
Cream and cheese fillings (dairy) are prepared in the same kitchen as the anko items, and the castella batter contains egg; no separation for vegan diners is documented.
Food offerings (toast, morning set) use butter and egg; no dairy-free or vegan options are documented, so only black coffee is reliably plant-based.
Coffee is self-roasted and brewed nel-drip; plain black coffee is naturally gluten-free and vegan.

name: ねぎ庵 流川店 (Negian Nagarekawa-ten)

claims.text: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki uses a wheat-flour batter and wheat noodles cooked on a shared teppan griddle, making cross-contact with gluten unavoidable.
Teppanyaki and okonomiyaki dishes are seasoned with standard sauces and soy sauce, which contain wheat.
Dishes are prepared on a shared griddle with pork, egg, oysters, and beef, so vegan separation is not provided.
An English menu is available, which helps travelers identify ingredients before ordering.
